text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- STATE OFFICIAL SAYS IMPOSSIBLE TO SELL BANESPA

Sao Paulo state's Finance Secretary Yoshiaki Nakano said it is impossible to privatise state bank Banespa due to a lack of interested buyers. Officials have spoken with 21 foreign and national banks and none are interested, he said.
-- TRADE DEFICIT HITS $655 MLN, AFFECTS EXCHANGE RATE
Brazil's trade deficit reached $655 million in September, its highest monthly figure since June 1995. The result was due to a rise in oil imports by state oil firm Petrobras.
-- ARGENTINA CLOSES DOOR TO BRAZILIAN BANKS

The Argentine government has decided to toughen its until-now flexible stance with Brazil regarding the opening of new banks in Argentina, saying only financial institutions which strictly meet all legal requirements may open branches there.
O GLOBO
-- STATE FIRMS TO LAY OFF 25,000 RETIREES STILL ON JOB
Brazilian state firms will lay off 25,000 pensioners still on the job. They will join 94,000 who lost posts due to last week's federal cost-cutting and revenue-boosting measures.
-- FEDERAL BANK FREES MONEY FOR NEW BUSINESSES
Brazilian federal bank Caixa Economica Federal will begin making available on Nov. 12 loans to recently formed and small businesses in the informal sector.
-- MODEL CLAUDIA APPEARS: "IT'S OVER. I'M ALIVE."

Eight days after entering a coma due to complications from anesthesia, top Brazilian model Claudia Liz appeared yesterday, wearing make-up and pyjamas, on her hospital room balcony.Asked how she felt, she said: "Great and I'm crazy to go home."
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- TRADE DEFICIT IS YEAR'S BIGGEST MONTHLY GAP
Brazil in September posted its biggest monthly trade deficit since June 1995, with imports exceeding exports by $655 million due mostly to a 50.8 percent hike in overseas oil purchases.
-- STATES TO PROPOSE 3-MONTH MORATORIUM ON DEBT PAYMENTS

Brazilian state governors will propose to President Fernando Henrique Cardoso a three-month suspension of debt payments, something the federal government has already approved to in the case of Mato Grosso state.
-- RONALDINHO SCORES THREE GOALS AND BRAZIL WINS
Brazil's national soccer team defeated Lithuania 3-1 in last night's friendly in Teresina. Ronaldinho, who plays for Spain's Barcelona, was the star of the night, scoring three goals.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
